newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African gold mines face crisis after dismal Q1.
newsitem.headline: S.African gold mines face crisis after dismal Q1.

text.p: Disastrous first quarter results and a sickly bullion price have hurled more South African gold mines into the marginal camp and hacked operating margins to their lowest level ever, analysts said on Tuesday.
Analysts say the industry needs a major face-lift to improve productivity and is fast approaching severe job cuts.
After years of belt-tightening in the face of slipping output, ageing mines and declining grades, this is the worst crisis to face the industry ever, analysts say.
"It has been an exceptionally bad quarter. Margins are down to 14 percent, the lowest in the history of gold mining in South Africa," said an analyst who asked not to be identified.
"The industry is in need of a major shake-out," he said.

Of the five mining houses that have so far reported first quarter results, only Gengold Ltd raised profits in the three months to end-March and that mainly because of a tax rebate and money from the cancellation of consulting service fees at one of its mines.
The rest suffered reduced earnings with JCI Ltd's profit cut by 67 percent on the preceding quarter.
Avgold Ltd is due to report at 1300 GMT.

The industry's circumstances are unlikely to brighten in the current June quarter with the Easter holiday break, two public holidays this week, a half-day nationwide strike on May 12 and a still fragile bullion price all taking their toll.
"The industry as a whole could be running at a loss in the June quarter. The average loss could be 70 rand an ounce next quarter," said Nick Goodwin, analyst at Fedsure Asset Management.
Another analyst said margins could drop to around 11 percent in the June quarter.

The world's largest gold producer, Anglo American Corp of South Africa Ltd, has already warned of shaft closures and retrenchments at two of its mines, Free State Consolidated Gold Mines Ltd and Vaal Reefs Exploration and Mining Co Ltd.

Blaming delays in implementing productivity agreements and poor management for declining productivity, analysts say that about 40 percent of gold mining production in South Africa is unprofitable -- and that before capital expenditure.
"It's getting quite disastrous. The mines will be threatened with closure. To survive they would have to drop production and go for higher grades. That means fewer people," Goodwin said.
Goodwin said that of the 40 gold mines in South Africa, employing about 350,000 people, 23 mines would become unpay (unprofitable) under the current average gold price of 1,500 rand/kg.
"That means about 1.5 million dependents with their income threatened. I cannot remember a worse situation in the mines' history," he said.

The mines held the weaker gold price mostly responsible for lower profits. The dollar bullion price has fallen since the start of the year and is seen heading towards a four-year low. It was last bid at $339 an ounce.
A steadier rand has removed any support the industry might receive from a higher rand gold price.
But analysts say the metal price is a variable and cannot be banked on. They say it is up to the mining houses, management and labour to rescue the industry from its current crisis.
